newsitem.title: USA: Amoco sees record earnings, raises dividend.
newsitem.headline: Amoco sees record earnings, raises dividend.

text.p: Amoco Corp. said Tuesday it will report record 1996 earnings and said it planned to repurchase up to $2 billion in common stock over the next two years.
In announcing the earnings projections, Amoco said it raised its annual dividend to $2.80 per share for 1997 from $2.60 per share for 1996.
"We will enjoy record earnings in 1996," said Amoco Chairman Laurance Fuller, without being more specific.
"We have achieved many of the benefits of our early-1990s restructurings and will continue to reap those benefits with new financial systems and process improvements," he said.
In 1995, Amoco earned $1.86 billion, or $3.76 a share.
The Chicago-based company said it set a goal of 10 percent annual earnings growth.

The dividend increase equalled raising the quarterly payout to 70 cents per share for the first quarter from the preceding quarter's rate of 65 cents per share, the company said, and is Amoco's third consecutive annual increase.
Anticipated capital and exploration spending of $4.1 billion for 1997 is below the estimated $4.5 billion the company will spend this year, Amoco said.
About $2.7 billion, or 65 percent, of 1997 spending was planned for worldwide exploration and production activity, more than half of which will be spent outside North America, the company said.
Key growth areas include Trinidad, Venezuela, Colombia, Azerbaijan, Egypt, the North Sea and the deep-water Gulf of Mexico.
Amoco's stock rose $1.625 to $77.50 Tuesday on the New York Stock Exchange.
